question: What does an electroencephalography (EEG) test actually measure?

options.A: Oxygen saturation levels in brain tissue
options.D: Blood flow velocity in brain vessels

explanation: Think of an EEG like a smart sensor that picks up the tiny electrical signals your brain cells make as they talk to each other! It's a great, painless way to see how the brain is functioning. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h1)

question: A healthy adult client closes their eyes and relaxes quietly. Which brain wave pattern is most likely to become dominant?
explanation: When you close your eyes and just chill out, your brain shifts into alpha wave mode. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the main reason a doctor would order an EEG test?

options.A: Locating tumors in the spinal column
options.D: Measuring pressure inside the eye chambers

explanation: EEGs are most commonly used to catch those tricky abnormal electrical patterns linked with epilepsy and seizures. Super important clinical tool! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h2)

question: A patient in the intensive care unit is being evaluated for potential brain death. Which test is routinely used to confirm this?
explanation: When doctors need to check for remaining brain activity in severe cases, a completely flatline EEG (cerebral silence) helps confirm brain death. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h2)

question: What common drink or food substance must a client avoid before having an EEG?
explanation: Caffeine is a little energy booster that stimulates the nervous system and can mess with normal brain waves during the test. Best to skip the coffee beforehand! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why should a client wash their hair thoroughly before coming in for an EEG?

options.A: To prevent the client from catching a scalp infection
options.B: To make the hair grow faster after the sticky paste is applied
options.C: To remove oils and hair products that block electrode contact
options.D: To cool down the scalp so the metal discs stick better

explanation: Hair gels, oils, and sprays create a barrier that stops the EEG electrodes from making good electrical contact with the scalp. Clean hair makes for a clear test! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the purpose of flashing lights (photic stimulation) during an EEG?

options.A: To warm up the conductive paste on the scalp
options.B: To trigger abnormal brain waves using flashing lights
options.C: To measure how fast the pupils dilate in bright light
options.D: To help the client relax into a deep sleep state

explanation: Sometimes brains need a little nudge to show what they do under stress. Flashing lights at different speeds can help bring out hidden seizure patterns. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h4)

question: During an EEG, the technician asks the client to breathe deeply and fast (hyperventilation). What happens in the body when you do this?

options.A: Build-up of lactic acid in the scalp muscles
options.B: Sudden expansion of fluid within brain ventricles
options.C: Increased oxygen levels and rapid heart deceleration
options.D: Decreased carbon dioxide and blood vessel constriction

explanation: Blowing off too much carbon dioxide makes your brain blood vessels tighten up a bit, which is a clever trick to help reveal hidden seizure activity on the screen. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is an important nursing duty right after a client finishes their EEG?

options.A: Ensuring regular seizure medications are resumed promptly
options.B: Keeping the client awake for another twelve hours
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent water intoxication
options.D: Applying fresh adhesive paste back onto the scalp

explanation: If any regular meds (especially seizure meds) were paused for the test, make sure to get them back on board right away to keep the patient safe! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h5)

question: A client looks in the mirror after an EEG and feels upset because their hair is messy with sticky paste. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Help the client wash their hair with warm water and shampoo
options.B: Ask the physician to write an order for a scalp scrub
options.C: Apply rubbing alcohol to dissolve the paste quickly
options.D: Tell the client the paste will wash off on its own tomorrow

explanation: That electrode paste can be super sticky and stubborn! Helping the patient clean up shows great bedside manner and restores their comfort. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why might a client with a true seizure disorder still have a completely normal EEG result?

options.A: The electrodes were placed on the wrong side of the forehead
options.B: Abnormal electrical activity may not happen during the recording period
options.C: The recording machine can only detect slow wave patterns
options.D: Anticonvulsant medications permanently cure abnormal brain waves

explanation: An EEG is just a snapshot in time. A patient can have epilepsy and still have a totally quiet, normal EEG when the machine happens to be recording! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which of the following findings on an EEG report is considered abnormal and concerning?

options.C: Delta waves during deep sleep stages
options.D: Alpha waves during quiet eye closure

explanation: Spikes and sharp waves where they shouldn't be are classic red flags that point toward an irritated spot in the brain or an active seizure focus. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h6)
